translation_notes: The five reads are five single-pattern m{ } with the predicate interpolated ({self.basens["hasNodeId"]}); next(g.objects(s, p), default) is `.first(default=xsd:anyType)`, next(g.objects(s, p)) with no default is the faithful `next(iter(m{ … }))` (raises StopIteration like the original; `.first()` would return None and let a missing hasNodeId through). The chain ns -> nsuri is NOT fused into a join: the original consumes the FIRST namespace only, a join would find another namespace that has a hasUri instead of raising (ldpy/016 pitfall).

The six .add() on self.bindingsg are one +{ } (add_run_shared_subject): five triples share the subject {mapiri}, the sixth has {attribute_iri} as subject; order of adds is immaterial in a graph. `@graph g` for the reads then `@graph self.bindingsg` for the write: two successive designations in one block. RDF["type"] becomes `a`. The draft`s `self.bindingsg += g{ }` was dropped: a fresh graph merged into the target is the add_isolated pattern, not this one.

Context shim opcua_lib_utils.py: idtype2String copied verbatim from semantic-model/opcua/lib/utils.py@3b40088b88 (fetched with gh); original.py edited only on its import line (`import lib.utils as utils` -> `import opcua_lib_utils as utils`), translated.ldpy has the same. `self` is the driver-local Bindings with the __init__ of bindings.py verbatim; basens is the real base.ttl namespace.
The map IRI is drawn with random.choices: the driver seeds `random` in each call (each side runs in its own forked process), so both draw the same name.
